standard_prerequisites.name: Finite presentation of the ring map R -> A and of the module M relative to A
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies both presentations whose relation matrices are spliced into the single presentation over R.

standard_prerequisites.name: Lifting elements of A[x_1, ..., x_n] to R[y_1, ..., y_m, x_1, ..., x_n]
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the entries h'_ij that let the A-presentation be rewritten as a presentation over R.

core_obligations: Choose a surjection A[x_1, ..., x_n] -> B and a presentation A[x_1, ..., x_n]^{oplus s} -> A[x_1, ..., x_n]^{oplus t} -> M -> 0 given by a matrix (h_ij), using that M is finitely presented relative to A (proof lines 21109-21115).
Choose a presentation A = R[y_1, ..., y_m]/(g_1, ..., g_u), using that A is of finite presentation over R (proof lines 21115-21118).
Lift the entries h_ij to elements h'_ij of R[y_1, ..., y_m, x_1, ..., x_n] (proof lines 21119-21120).

Form the t x (s + t u) presentation matrix over R[y_1, ..., y_m, x_1, ..., x_n] whose first t x s block is h'_ij and whose remaining u blocks of size t x t are g_i I_t, and conclude that it presents M over R (proof lines 21120-21127).
difficulty_reason: The lemma works with finite type ring maps R -> A -> B, a B-module M that is finitely presented relative to A, and assumes that A is of finite presentation over R; the conclusion is that M is finitely presented relative to R (source lines 21101-21106). The proof has to choose two presentations, one of B over A and one of M over A[x_1, ..., x_n], and additionally a presentation A = R[y_1, ..., y_m]/(g_1, ..., g_u) (proof lines 21108-21119). The substantive step is lifting the entries h_ij of the A[x]-relation matrix to elements h'_ij of R[y_1, ..., y_m, x_1, ..., x_n] and then assembling a single t x (s + t u) presentation matrix over R by appending u blocks g_i I_t (proof lines 21119-21127). The author states the resulting presentation without verifying that its cokernel is M, so the bookkeeping of the blocks is the content left to the reader.
